Moreover, any unclear incorporation of the term must be construed against PeakFit, favoring enforceability of the promise. issues.question: Is the £2,000 promise a binding term of contract or merely marketing puff by PeakFit?

candidates.query: advertisement promise term contract marketing puff binding intention
candidates.reason: This issue is whether the £2,000 promise is a contractual term or mere marketing puff. Carlill (J23) supports enforceability when intention to be bound is clear, Central London Property Trust v High Trees (J33) reinforces that promises intended to be binding and acted upon can create obligations. Merritt v Merritt (J30) and Balfour v Balfour (J29) distinguish intention in social/domestic agreements. Partridge v Crittenden (J24) is relevant for advertisement context.
